references.text: The Lord gives Moses the task of leading the children of Israel out of Egypt, which is repeated here in 6:13.
Aaron is appointed to be Moses' spokesman, and both receive the command together here.
The Lord repeats the commission to Moses and Aaron to speak to Pharaoh so that he will let the children of Israel go.
Fulfillment of the command: Pharaoh finally lets the children of Israel leave Egypt.
Moses led the children of Israel out of Egypt according to the Lord's command, as a fulfillment of this verse.
The psalm confirms that Moses and Aaron led God's people like a flock out of Egypt.
The Lord sent Moses, his servant, and Aaron whom he had chosen, to carry out his will in Egypt.
Moses was faithful in all God's house, which refers to his obedience to the command to lead the people out.
Stephen refers to God sending Moses as leader and deliverer to bring the people out of Egypt.
Verse 27 confirms and summarizes that Moses and Aaron carried out the specific command given in verse 13.
Verse 26 confirms the identity of those who received the command in verse 13 and emphasizes the military/organizational scope of the mission.
Verse 29 elaborates on the source and authority behind the command given in verse 13 by linking it directly to God's name and word.
Verse 7:2 clarifies the roles in the mission from verse 13 by distinguishing between the recipient of God's word (Moses) and the speaker to Pharaoh (Aaron).
Verse 7:1 provides the theological premise (God's strong hand) that enables the command in verse 13 to be fulfilled.
